source.title: Drug-related problems in hospitalised Parkinson’s disease patients in China

extraction.batching: Not required: 5-page primary article with one figure and four tables was mapped and reviewed as one semantic unit.

duplicate_review.finding: No duplicate atoms detected by deterministic atom_id/canonical statement review.

consistency_findings.finding: Three incompatible distributions are reported: abstract 88.7% B-D / 11.3% E-H; Results/Table 3 85.4% (234/274) / 14.6% (40/274); discussion 82.5% / 17.5%.
consistency_findings.handling: Retained as separate source-reported atoms; not reconciled. Table 3 is arithmetically consistent with its explicit counts, but this does not justify silently correcting the other sections.

consistency_findings.finding: Narrative reports 89.9% (218/224) B-D and 15.0% (6/40) E-H. 218/224 is 97.3%, while 6/40 uses all E-H events rather than C1 as denominator.
consistency_findings.handling: Flagged as a source inconsistency; no corrected atom created.

consistency_findings.finding: The reported total mean length of stay (6.1 days) is lower than both DRP subgroups (11.0 and 10.2 days); the reported total PD duration (10.8 years) is higher than both subgroup means (8.0 and 5.5 years).
consistency_findings.handling: Values are preserved in SEA as reported and flagged; no inferred correction.

consistency_findings.finding: Discussion says “Drug selection, C1” and “Treatment duration, C3” accounted for over 90%, but Table 3 defines C3 as Dose selection and C4 as Treatment duration.
consistency_findings.handling: Flagged as terminology inconsistency; Table 3 labels retained for extracted cause atoms.

consistency_findings.finding: Conclusion states PD patients were more likely to be non-adherent, especially to levodopa, while Methods state medication compliance could not be comprehensively identified and patient-related causes were excluded.
consistency_findings.handling: Conclusion preserved as an author-conclusion atom with needs_review status; not treated as an observed result.

consistency_findings.finding: The DRP percentages (e.g. levodopa 30 [69.8%]) are not explained as rates among medication users; 30/209 is not 69.8%.
consistency_findings.handling: Atoms structure the DRP count only and retain the source-reported percentage in text without interpreting its denominator.

extraction_limitations: Figure 1 provides a ranked bar chart without printed exact percentages for each category; only the ranking was atomised.

The current schema requires an exposure context for quantitative_result atoms. Broad study-level DRP prevalence/cause results therefore use a source-supported generic exposure descriptor (“Hospital pharmacotherapy during the index Parkinson’s disease admission”).
No correction was made for internally inconsistent source percentages, table values, labels, or denominators.
Bibliographic references were not atomised; they were routed to the separate reference task queue.
schema_gaps: The schema has no dedicated descriptive-prevalence result kind that does not require an exposure, so descriptive hospital DRP results require a broad exposure descriptor.
The schema cannot directly represent a multi-category frequency distribution in one quantitative result except through arm observations or multiple atoms.
